14. The petitioner further submits that there are other creditors like Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Jananta Bank, IFIC, ICB, etc, but the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank has the first charge over respondent companies properties as it has legal mortgage. Both Shilpa Bank and Janata Bank had filed money suits which were decreed in their favour but the decrees could not be executed as no purchaser of the respondent company could be found. The petitioner also filed Money Suit No. 66 of 1995 which is now pending. But there is no possibility of recovering its unsecured loan since Shilpa Bank loan is not only for a large amount but also a secured one. The petitioner further submits that the total liabilities of the respondent are more than its assets. 

 21. He has drawn my attention to the failure to execute the decree obtained by Shilpa Bank, against the respondent, for non-availability of a purchaser and also to the government policy, under which the respondent company is given twelve years to repay the loan taken from the Shilpa Bank.
